newsitem.title: UK: UK's Airtech valued at 31 mln stg after placing.
newsitem.headline: UK's Airtech valued at 31 mln stg after placing.

text.p: The UK's Airtech, whose principal product is a masthead amplifier that enhances the coverage of base stations within a cellular mobile telecoms network, said it was valued at 30.97 million stg after a placing.

The Buckinghamshire-based company, which published its prospectus for its flotation on the Alternative Investment Market, placed 35.5 percent of its ordinary shares at 68 pence each to raise 10.35 million stg.
The shares are expected to start trade on October 3.

Airtech, which posted a full year loss of 230,000 stg in the year to December 1995, on sales of 2.8 million stg, said the global cellular communications market in which it operated was one of the fastest growing and most technologically advanced.

Airtech, whose products and future products are based on "a clear understanding" of modern digital wireless technology, is working with companies such as the U.S.'s Motorola Inc and Finland's Nokia Ab, Oy.
It said it had won orders worth more than nine million stg for its masthead amplifier and saw further significant orders.

These amplifiers are installed directly beneath the antennae so that the base station can receive signals that may otherwise have been lost. They also have a particularly sensitive filter and low noise amplifier which selects and boosts the received signal from the mobile telephones to the base station.

"The directors believe Airtech has the opportunity and capability to become a leading supplier of products and services designed to enhance the performance of modern cellular communications networks throughout the world," it stated.
In February, Airtech set up a U.S. operation, AWS Inc, in Texas, through which it hopes to exploit the U.S. market.

With the market for base stations and associated equipment driven by demand for mobile telephones, Airtech said that according to independent consultants, the number of world-wide mobile telephone subscribers is expected to grow from a current level of over 100 million to around 295 million by 2000.
